newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN LAW COMMISSION BACKS CONTINGENCY FEES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN LAW COMMISSION BACKS CONTINGENCY FEES.

text.p: The South African Law Commission has recommended that contingency fee agreements for lawyers should be legalised.
In a report tabled in parliament on Monday, the commission said that introducing contingency fees would increase access to the court system by more South Africans.
A contingency fee agreement between a lawyer and clients allows for the lawyer not to charge any fees if the client's court case is unsuccessful.
"The system therefore implies that a litigant may, in certain instances, instruct a legal practitioner on a 'no success, no pay' basis," the commission said.

"Up to the present such a system has not been recognised in South African law due to common law restraints. It has, however, been introduced in certain legal systems abroad, mainly because of its enormous potential to promote access to justice."
Should a case be won, the fees paid to the lawyer could be recovered from the proceeds of the litigation and would normally be higher that the lawyer's normal fees.
"This is so because the legal practitioner bears the risk of not being compensated in a number of cases," the commission said.
In view of this, the commission said payments should be limited to a maximum of 100 percent of normal fees and should not exceed 25 percent of the proceeds of litigations.
The commission said it did not believe that contingency fee agreement should be allowed in family law cases, in order not to encourage certain types of litigation, such as divorce.
This should also not be allowed in criminal law cases as people accused of crime were adequately catered for in the constitution.

"In view of reservations that contingency fee agreements may lead to an increase in frivolous litigation, the commission recommends that contingency fee agreements should only be entered into in cases where there are reasonable prospects that the client's case will be successful," it said.
